text: Martin mentioned customers are noticing the slowness. What specific feedback or complaint data have you seen in the last month that tells you this is a problem?
why: Validates the urgency with real evidence and reveals whether there are metrics tracking customer dissatisfaction

text: What percentage of applications are you currently deciding within the 3-day promise, and what percentage are taking longer?
why: Establishes the baseline performance and the scale of the gap between promise and reality

text: If we could reduce check times, which outcome matters most to Martin: faster decisions for customers, reduced cost per application, or freeing up analyst time for complex cases?
why: Clarifies the primary success metric when trade-offs arise during design

text: Tom, walk me through the last personal account application you worked on yesterday. What did you look at, what did you check, and how long did each part take?
why: Gets a concrete, recent example of the actual workflow with real time estimates, not idealized process

text: When you open a passport or driving licence image, what specifically are you checking for, and what makes you decide it's acceptable versus needing to escalate or reject it?
why: Uncovers the decision rules and edge cases that an AI system would need to replicate

text: Of the 1,900 weekly applications, roughly how many get approved on first review, how many need more documents requested, and how many get escalated to Financial Crime?
why: Reveals the distribution of complexity and identifies which path offers the biggest time-saving opportunity

text: What happens after you request additional documents from a customer? How long does that loop typically add, and how many times does it happen per application on average?
why: Identifies whether rework loops are a major source of delay and whether better upfront guidance could help

text: What format are the uploaded documents stored in, and can you show me three examples of a passport, a utility bill, and a proof of address that were approved last week?
why: Confirms image quality, file formats, and whether the data is suitable for document AI processing

text: Does the case management system record timestamps for when an analyst opens a case, requests documents, or makes a decision? Can we export that data for the last six months?
why: Determines whether we can measure current performance and build a baseline for comparison

text: Who can grant us read-only access to the case management system and document storage, and how long does that approval process typically take here?
why: Identifies the path to data access and whether the six-week timeline is realistic given internal processes

text: Helen, what would cause you to say no to a change in the KYC process? Are there specific regulatory requirements or audit findings that we must not put at risk?
why: Surfaces non-negotiable constraints early, before we design something that cannot be approved

text: If an AI system flagged a document as likely acceptable, but an analyst still makes the final decision, would that be acceptable from a regulatory perspective?
why: Tests whether an AI-assisted model is viable or whether full human review is mandatory

text: Have you had any regulatory findings, internal audit issues, or near-misses in KYC in the past year that we should be aware of?
why: Identifies recent pain points that will shape what the MLRO will and will not tolerate in a new system

text: At the end of the six-week pilot, what would Martin need to see in terms of numbers—speed, accuracy, volume processed—to consider this a success and worth rolling out?
why: Defines the quantitative bar for pilot success so we can design to meet it

text: Deborah, if we pilot this with a subset of your team, which analysts would you want involved, and what would make them trust and actually use the new tool day-to-day?
why: Identifies user adoption risks and the conditions needed for the team to embrace rather than resist the change
